title: Sonquoequahesick / Sonnquoquas
summary: Sonquoequahesick, also Sonnquoquas, is associated with Sonquoqua and Tom's Creek on Hashamomuk Neck in Southold.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Corchaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The Algonquian name Sonquoequahesick preserves the identity of Sonquoqua, a prominent Manhansett leader who lived along the creek and signed the 1652 deed for Shelter Island 1 2 . Reclaiming these specific, personal geographic markers ensures that the deep, enduring histories of Native families remain permanently anchored within the modern Long Island landscape.
introduction_content: Sonnquoquas is recorded as a name for Tom's Creek, or land adjoining it, at Southold.
history_content: The name is connected with Sonquoqua, a Manhansett leader whose English name Tom may have given Tom's Creek its later English name. The map placement is a general Tom's Creek / Hashamomuk Neck placement.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Sonnquoquas, Sonquoqua, Sonquoequahesick, and Sonquoequashissick. The name is treated as a personal name with a brook-related locative form.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are of great historical and contemporary significance for Indigenous Communities. Place names carry importance in Indigenous cultures because they are reflections of creation stories, history and teachings, and markers of navigational information, environmental and ecological knowledge.”

— Geographical Names Board of Canada, Environmental Scan of Indigenous Toponymic Activities in Canada (2021), PDF page 61, Appendix A
preservation_content: Sonquoequahesick connects a named Native person, a creek, and the Shelter Island and Southold record landscape, preserving more than a geographic label alone.
